text: Why must those who know him look in vain for such days?
they pasture flocks they have stolen.
and take the widow’s ox in pledge.
and force all the poor of the land into hiding.
the poor go about their labor of foraging food; the wasteland provides food for their children.
and glean in the vineyards of the wicked.
they have nothing to cover themselves in the cold.
and hug the rocks for lack of shelter.
the infant of the poor is seized for a debt.
they carry the sheaves, but still go hungry.
they tread the winepresses, yet suffer thirst.
and the souls of the wounded cry out for help. But God charges no one with wrongdoing.
who do not know its ways or stay in its paths.
and kills the poor and needy; in the night he steals forth like a thief.
he thinks, ‘No eye will see me,’ and he keeps his face concealed.
but by day they shut themselves in; they want nothing to do with the light.
they make friends with the terrors of darkness.
their portion of the land is cursed, so that no one goes to the vineyards.
so the grave snatches away those who have sinned.
the worm feasts on them; evil men are no longer remembered but are broken like a tree.
and to the widow show no kindness.
though they become established, they have no assurance of life.
but his eyes are on their ways.
they are brought low and gathered up like all others; they are cut off like heads of grain.
and reduce my words to nothing?”
